chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr and Muhammad ibn Isma'il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan and Ibn Abi Umayr and a number of our companions from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah and Hammam ibn Isa, all from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you have finished your Sa'y while you are in the state of Tamattu', shorten your hair from its sides and your beard, trim your mustache, and clip your nails, and keep them for your Hajj. When you do that, you have exited the state of Ihram from everything from which the Muhrim exits, and you have entered Ihram for it, and circumambulate the House as a voluntary prayer as much as you wish.

key_terms.سَعْيٌ: Sa'y (ritual walking between Safa and Marwah)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific grooming rituals and legal status changes for a pilgrim performing Hajj al-Tamattu' after Sa'y?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific grooming rituals—trimming hair, beard, mustache, and nails—that mark the transition from the restricted state of Ihram to full permissibility for a Mutamatti' pilgrim after completing the Sa'y. Scholarly tradition emphasizes that these acts are not merely hygienic but serve as the definitive legal signal that the pilgrim is released from Ihram prohibitions, allowing for voluntary Tawaf and the commencement of the Umrah rites.
